Before we start

What your business needs in place.

None of this is code, and each one blocks a launch.

A commercial registration, for payments

Payment gateways in Egypt and Saudi will not settle to an individual. Getting the CR or working through an existing entity is the longest lead time in the whole launch, so it starts before anything else.

A business bank account

In the same legal name as the registration. Settlement fails at exactly the moment your first orders arrive if these do not match.

Product data somebody has actually written

Names, prices, weights, variants and images. Weights matter more than people expect — shipping is priced on them, and guessed weights turn into losses on every parcel.

A returns and shipping policy you will honour

Both stores and both regulators expect it published, and COD customers read it. Write the one you will actually follow, not the one that sounds generous.

Carrier accounts, or permission to open them

Egypt Post, Bosta, SMSA or whoever you ship with. Rates are negotiated per merchant, so this must be in your name to be worth anything.

Right fit, wrong fit

Saves a call that would end in no.

A good fit

  • You have products and no store that works
  • COD is most of your revenue and returns are eating it
  • You sell in Arabic and the storefront has to feel Arabic
  • You want to run it yourself afterwards
  • You are selling into Egypt or Saudi and want someone who has

Not a fit

  • You want a marketplace with many sellers — different build entirely
  • You need traffic more than you need a store
  • You have no products yet
  • You want a custom storefront from scratch when Shopify would do

After launch

After the store opens.

A store is not a project, it is a shop. Prices change, apps update and break, a carrier changes its rates, and a theme update quietly breaks the Arabic checkout. Every launch includes 30 days; the Care plan keeps someone in the shop after that.

Questions

The ones people actually ask.

Why Shopify rather than something custom?

Because payments, tax, inventory and checkout are solved problems that cost a fortune to rebuild badly. Custom makes sense when the business model is genuinely unusual — and then I will say so and quote the build instead.

Does the COD confirmation really reduce returns?

It reduces the refusals that come from a customer who forgot they ordered, changed their mind, or gave a wrong address — which is most of them. It does not fix a product problem, and the reporting will show you which of the two you have.

Can you migrate an existing store?

Yes — products, customers, orders and URL redirects so search rankings survive. The audit is the honest first step: sometimes migrating is the wrong answer and fixing what you have is cheaper.

Who pays Shopify?

You do, directly, on your own account. Same for the gateway and the carriers. I never sit between you and a subscription, and I take no commission from any of them.

Can I run it without a developer afterwards?

That is the point. The handover is a walkthrough of adding products, changing prices, running promotions and reading the reports. The Care plan is for when you would rather not.
